quotes.text: We’ve deprecated use of the Charges API to create card payments and plan to remove support.
New integrations can’t use the Charges API to create payments.
The Charges API doesn’t support the following features, many of which are required for credit card compliance:
If using both the Payment Intent and Charge objects, you’re not guaranteed to see consistent values for these fields.
Don’t store any sensitive information (personally identifiable information, card details, and so on) as metadata or in the charge’s `description` parameter.

old_evidence.text: The content of this section refers to a _Legacy_ (Technology that's no longer recommended) feature.
If using both the Payment Intent and Charge objects, you’re not guaranteed to see consistent values for these fields.

findings: The November page adds an explicit, scoped lifecycle status: use of Charges API to create card payments is deprecated, Stripe plans to remove support, and new integrations cannot use Charges API to create payments (new raw lines 5-25). The April page called Charges/Tokens legacy and recommended PaymentIntents for new integrations but did not say support was planned for removal or that new integration creation is barred (old raw lines 4-21). Neither page gives a removal date or proves existing charge retrieval/refund operations are removed.

The mapped multi-raw source says 'Charges + ACH APIs: unsupported but not being removed; no future development' (source-stripe-legacy-apis.md:23-26), directly conflicting with the November Charges card-payment-creation warning. Correct the Charges part with the exact new scope and date while preserving separate ACH and Sources claims as their own dated evidence; do not project this card-specific notice onto all Charges operations or legacy APIs.

Charges flow remains browser Elements collection, Stripe.js tokenization, token sent to merchant server, server Charge amount/currency and fulfillment only after successful payment. PaymentIntents flow uses a server-created Intent/client secret, client 3DS via Stripe.js/mobile SDK and success webhook before fulfillment (old raw lines 23-39; new raw lines 27-41). Token generation, API acceptance or charge creation alone is not a successful payment or fulfillment instruction.

Both captures retain charge-ID Refund creation/full-or-partial amount, legacy iOS Apple Pay PKPayment to Token to server Charge, dynamic statement descriptor constraints, Charge metadata and decline outcome/API error or charge.failed webhook (old raw lines 41-182; new raw lines 43-160). November swaps Node examples for curl in refunds, descriptor and metadata, preserving server secret-key boundary; it does not establish SDK deprecation or actual Apple Pay support for new Charges integration.

Both captures warn PaymentIntent and Charge metadata/description can differ and require updates to the Intent object when using Payment Intents (old raw lines 145-153; new raw lines 131-139). The summary source lines 40-46 omits that identity warning even though it summarizes Charges metadata; add it to prevent cross-object reconciliation errors.

Source frontmatter/Raw Sources list the April Charges raw among seven legacy captures but not November (source lines 1-14,128-136). Add exact canonical URL and November raw route specifically to the Charges section, retaining all other raw provenance. The company Stripe page's Charges API table also says unsupported but available/no future development (wiki/companies/stripe.md:175); flag a reciprocal dated warning rather than assume every table row is superseded.
substantive_changes: November states planned removal of support for Charges API card-payment creation and disallows new integrations using Charges API to create payments, beyond April's legacy/not-recommended language (old raw lines 8-21; new raw lines 5-25).
historical_claims_to_preserve: April 20, 2026 Charges/Tokens legacy and PaymentIntents recommendation, token-to-server Charge flow, Refund/Apple Pay/descriptor/metadata/decline examples remain dated technical evidence (old raw lines 4-182). New lifecycle notice narrows new card-payment creation but does not retroactively erase example content.

The multi-raw source's older Sources API and ACH status claims derive from separate raw routes and must not be generalized from the November Charges card-payment page (source-stripe-legacy-apis.md:6-14,23-26,128-136).
conflicts: source-stripe-legacy-apis.md:25 says Charges API is not being removed; November says Stripe plans to remove support for Charges API card-payment creation (new raw line 17). Add reciprocal dated/scope warning in that source and company table at wiki/companies/stripe.md:175, without asserting a removal date or blanket API shutdown.

The summary's legacy payment-method use table at source lines 47-54 can sound like Charges remain a choice for new US/Canada integrations, but November says new integrations cannot use Charges API to create payments (new raw line 17). Mark that table historical/legacy-only.
unresolved_questions: No removal date, migration cutoff, exact grandfathered access policy, or fate of Charges read/refund APIs is given by this page (new raw lines 15-25,43-60).
November still includes server Charge creation examples for existing legacy context; they do not override the explicit new-integration prohibition (new raw lines 17,100-150).

findings: Add exact Charges page URL and November raw route while retaining seven older legacy raw links (source lines 1-14,128-136; new raw lines 1-2).

Correct source line 25's broad Charges-not-being-removed language with November's planned removal of Charges card-payment creation and no new integration creation (new raw lines 15-25), leaving separate ACH status dated and unasserted by this page.

Date/qualify the source lines 47-54 Charges use-case table as existing legacy context only; retain charge-versus-Intent flow at lines 28-38 and add PaymentIntent-versus-Charge metadata/description identity warning (old raw lines 145-153; new raw lines 131-139).
conflicts: Source line 25 conflicts with new raw line 17 on Charges card-payment creation removal plan.
Source lines 47-54 imply new US/Canada Charges use despite new raw line 17's new-integration bar.
source_assessments.reason: The November page adds a material Charges card-payment lifecycle restriction and exposes a direct current-summary contradiction; other legacy API claims and existing-operation examples remain separately dated.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/charges-api, the November capture explicitly calls Charges API card-payment creation deprecated, says Stripe plans to remove support, and bars new integrations from using Charges API to create payments; it recommends Checkout or Payment Intents (new raw lines 5-25). The old April guide called Charges/Tokens legacy and recommended PaymentIntents but did not state that removal plan or bar (old raw lines 4-21). Both show a legacy browser Elements/Stripe.js Token sent to the merchant server for a Charge, versus a server-created PaymentIntent/client secret and client authentication, with fulfillment only after successful payment/webhook (old raw lines 23-39; new raw lines 27-41). The mapped source-stripe-legacy-apis.md incorrectly says Charges are not being removed and offers a historical US/Canada Charges use-case table without the new integration bar (source lines 23-25,47-54). It must keep ACH/Sources claims separate and date the Charges correction. Tokenization, charge creation and a client return do not establish payment success.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/charges-api, the substantive November change is the explicit plan to remove Charges API card-payment creation and the prohibition for new Charges payment integrations (old raw lines 8-21; new raw lines 15-25). Node-to-curl example changes for refunds, descriptors and metadata, reordered headings and replacement links are presentation; legacy Apple Pay PKPayment-to-Token and Charge-ID Refund examples remain dated and do not prove new-integration eligibility (old raw lines 41-175; new raw lines 43-153). source-stripe-legacy-apis.md needs dual raw provenance, a scoped contradiction warning for its 'not being removed' line 25 and a historical-only label on its Charges use-case table (source lines 1-14,23-25,47-54,128-136). Preserve the PaymentIntent versus Charge metadata/description identity distinction, server token/secret-key versus client authentication roles, and fulfillment-after-success state (old raw lines 23-39,145-153; new raw lines 27-41,131-139). No removal date or blanket shutdown of Charges retrieval/refunds or other legacy APIs follows.
